name: market_breadth_signal_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Market breadth — the proportion of stocks advancing vs declining — diverges from the headline NIFTY 50 index during distribution (narrow rally in 5-10 heavy-weight stocks while breadth deteriorates) and accumulation (broad-based buying while index is flat due to weakness in heavyweights). When NIFTY 50 makes a new intraday high but the advance-decline ratio is declining, it signals unsustainable narrowing and a likely reversal within 15-30 minutes. In Indian markets, this divergence is amplified because NIFTY 50 is top-heavy: top 10 stocks represent ~55% of weight. A rally in HDFC Bank + Reliance + TCS can push NIFTY up while 40 other stocks are flat or down. The inefficiency persists because most retail traders watch only the index level, not breadth metrics, and breadth data requires monitoring all 50 constituents simultaneously.
stock_filter: All NIFTY 50 constituents for breadth computation; trade via NIFTY 50 futures or NIFTYBEES

other: 1-min OHLCV for all 50 NIFTY constituents for breadth computation

indicators.name: advance_decline_ratio
indicators.formula: count(stocks where close > close[5]) / count(stocks where close < close[5])

conditions: breadth_ema > 1.2 (but majority of stocks are actually advancing)
long.confirmation: NIFTY 50 1-min close > NIFTY 50 1-min close[1] (first uptick from the low)

conditions: breadth_ema < 0.8 (but majority of stocks are actually declining)
short.confirmation: NIFTY 50 1-min close < NIFTY 50 1-min close[1] (first downtick from the high)

entry.entry_price: market order on NIFTY 50 futures at confirmation

exit.target: NIFTY 50 moves 20 bps in direction of breadth (reversal from divergence)
exit.stop_loss: NIFTY 50 makes another new high/low extending 10 bps beyond entry
exit.time_stop: exit after 30 bars (if divergence doesn't resolve, it may be a legitimate new trend)
exit.signal_exit: breadth_ema realigns with index direction (divergence resolved without reversal)

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L in NIFTY futures (1 mini lot if available) or NIFTYBEES

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; in high VIX, breadth divergences may not revert (panic selling)
filters.time_filter: skip first 15 min (breadth metrics need stabilization) and last 10 min
filters.trend_filter: divergence is more reliable when NIFTY is near day's VWAP (not extreme trend)
filters.event_filter: skip on broad macro event days (all stocks move together, breadth uninformative)
other_filters: require at least 30 of 50 stocks to have meaningful 5-min returns (exclude those halted or illiquid)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — breadth divergence is a classic technical analysis concept but its real-time intraday computation at 1-min resolution is novel. Most practitioners use daily breadth, not intraday.

weaknesses: Breadth divergence can persist for extended periods (2+ hours) before resolving. The 30-bar time stop may exit positions prematurely before the thesis plays out.
On days with heavy FII selling in large-caps only (e.g., MSCI rebalance), breadth divergence is genuine and NIFTY decline will persist despite positive breadth.
Computing real-time breadth for all 50 stocks requires monitoring 50 simultaneous data feeds, which is resource-intensive and may have data latency issues.
prior_art: Zweig (1986) 'Winning on Wall Street' popularized breadth indicators. McClellan Oscillator and Summation Index are classic breadth tools. In India, intraday breadth analysis is nascent — BSE/NSE publish daily A/D ratios but not intraday.
notes: The 5-bar lookback for advance/decline classification is a balance between responsiveness and noise. 1-bar lookback is too noisy; 10-bar lookback is too slow. Experiment with VWAP-based classification (advancing = close > VWAP, declining = close < VWAP) as an alternative to close-over-close.
